files.lesson.md: --- order: 1 unit: area node: AC9M7M01 n1 title: Area of parallelograms summary: "Cut a triangle off one end of a parallelogram and move it to the other end: it becomes a rectangle with the same base and height. So the area of a parallelogram is base × perpendicular height." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Tiles, bricks in a wall, and the stripes of a pedestrian crossing seen from an angle are parallelograms. How much area does a slanted tile cover?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8273 url: http://127.0.0.1:8273/index.html readySelector: "#sl-s" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: area.yml#explain-pic, caption: "The triangle cut off the left end fills the gap on the right: a 6 by 4 rectangle, so the parallelogram's area is $6 \\times 4 = 24$ cm²." } explainClip: query: { code: "@area.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Cut and move" say: "A parallelogram can be cut into a rectangle." clip: - caption: { text: "Cut a triangle off the left end.", say: "Cut a triangle off the left end." } - click: Cut and move - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "6 × 4 = 24" } - wait: 600 - caption: { text: "It fills the gap: a 6 by 4 rectangle.", say: "It fills the gap on the right: a rectangle." } - wait: 1000 - click: Put the piece back - caption: { text: "Slide the top along: same base, same height, same area.", say: "Slide the top along. The area stays the same." } - click: Move the top right - click: Move the top right - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "= 24" } - wait: 1200 --- The **area** of a shape is how many unit squares it covers. A rectangle 5 cm long and 3 cm high has 3 rows of 5 squares: $5 \times 3 = 15$ square centimetres, written 15 cm². A **parallelogram** has two pairs of parallel sides, like a rectangle pushed over. Its **base** is one side, and its **perpendicular height** is the distance straight up from the base to the opposite side, at a right angle (marked ∟). The slanted side is longer than the height. ## Predict: pushed over ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to which shape covers more surfaces the belief that the slanted sides, being longer, add area." check: type: predict q: "A rectangle and a parallelogram both have base 6 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm. Which covers more area?" options: ["They cover the same area", "The parallelogram: its slanted sides are longer", "The rectangle: it is not pushed over"] actual: "The same: 24 cm² each. Cut a triangle off the parallelogram and move it, and it becomes the 6 by 4 rectangle." ``` Picture the parallelogram as the rectangle pushed over. Does anything get added or taken away? ## Run: cut and move ```step stage: run insight: "Cutting off the triangle and moving it shows the parallelogram rearranges into a rectangle with the same base and height." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#run", height: 520 } check: { type: board, text: "Press **Cut and move**. What shape do you get, and what is its area? Was your prediction right?", when: "c = 1", explain: "A 6 by 4 rectangle: 24 cm². Nothing was added or lost, only moved." } ``` The dashed orange line is the perpendicular height. The cut goes along it. ## Investigate: base times height ```step stage: investigate insight: "Area = base × perpendicular height; Ruby's mistake uses the slanted side, which is longer than the height." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "A parallelogram has base 8 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm. What is its area, in cm²?" answer: "40" feedback: - ["13", "That adds. Area is base × height."] - ["26", "That is twice (8 + 5): a perimeter idea. Area is base × height."] explain: "8 × 5 = 40 cm²." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ruby" text: "Ruby finds the area of a parallelogram. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: slant-height explain: "Line 3: 5 cm is the slanted side, not the height. The height is the perpendicular distance, 4 cm: 7 × 4 = 28 cm²." - check: type: question q: "Why does a parallelogram have the same area as a rectangle with the same base and height?" options: ["The triangle cut off one end fits exactly into the gap at the other end", "Its slanted sides are the same length as the rectangle's sides", "Both shapes have four sides"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The slanted sides are longer than the height, so that is not it.", "Many four-sided shapes have different areas."] explain: "Cut along the height and move the triangle: the parallelogram becomes the rectangle, with nothing added or lost." ``` ### Cut, move, multiply Here is why the formula works, then how to use it. ```worked A = 6 \times 4 = 24 \text{ cm}^2 :: A rectangle: 4 rows of 6 unit squares. \text{parallelogram} \to \text{rectangle} :: Cut along the height and move the triangle: the same base and height. A = b \times h :: So a parallelogram's area is base × perpendicular height. A = 8 \times 5 = 40 \text{ cm}^2 :: Use the height at a right angle to the base, never the slanted side. ``` Now try one: base 8 cm, height 5 cm. ### Find the mistake Read Ruby's working. Which length is at a right angle to the base? ### Why it works ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: sliding the top to make a rectangle, building an area from a base, a decimal height, finding a missing height (backwards), then the edge case of a very slanted parallelogram." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#straighten", height: 520 } tasks: - starter: "area.yml#straighten" hint: "Move the top until it sits straight above the left end of the base." check: { type: board, text: "Slide the top until the parallelogram is a rectangle. Did the area change?", when: "s = 0", explain: "s = 0 puts the top straight above: a rectangle, still 6 × 4 = 24 cm²." } - starter: "area.yml#twentyfour" hint: ["Which number times 8 makes 24?", "Set b to 8 first."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a parallelogram with base 8 cm and area 24 cm².", when: "b = 8 and a = 24", explain: "8 × 3 = 24, so the height is 3 cm." } - check: type: answer q: "A parallelogram has base 12 m and perpendicular height 3.5 m. What is its area, in m²?" answer: "42" feedback: - ["15.5", "That adds. Multiply the base by the height."] explain: "12 × 3.5 = 42 m² (12 × 3 = 36, plus 12 × 0.5 = 6)." - check: type: answer q: "A parallelogram has area 30 cm² and base 6 cm. What is its perpendicular height, in cm?" answer: "5" feedback: - ["180", "That multiplies. Which number times 6 makes 30?"] - ["24", "That subtracts. Area = base × height, so divide."] explain: "6 × h = 30, so h = 30 ÷ 6 = 5 cm." - check: type: question q: "Edge case: two parallelograms both have base 5 cm and height 3 cm. One is very slanted. Which has the bigger area?" options: ["Neither: both are 15 cm²", "The very slanted one", "The less slanted one"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Slanting makes the sides longer but keeps the height.", "Same base, same height, same area."] explain: "Area depends only on the base and the perpendicular height: 5 × 3 = 15 cm² for both." ``` ### Straighten it Each task changes one thing. ### Area 24 ### A decimal height ### Backwards: the height ### Very slanted ## Practise: parallelograms ```step stage: practise insight: "Whole and decimal bases, units, and a slanted side to ignore, mixed; the review keeps decimal multiplication fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Base 9 cm, perpendicular height 7 cm. Area, in cm²?" answer: "63" feedback: - ["16", "That adds."] explain: "9 × 7 = 63 cm²." - check: type: answer q: "A parallelogram has base 10 cm, slanted side 6 cm and perpendicular height 4.5 cm. Area, in cm²?" answer: "45" feedback: - ["60", "6 cm is the slanted side. Use the height, 4.5 cm."] explain: "10 × 4.5 = 45 cm²." smaller: check: { type: question, q: "Cut the triangle off one end and move it, and the slanted side is gone. Which length is left as the rectangle's side: 6 cm or 4.5 cm?", options: ["6 cm", "4.5 cm"], answer: 1, explain: "The cut goes straight down, at a right angle to the base, so the height 4.5 cm is the rectangle's side. The slanted side disappears." } - check: type: question q: "A parallelogram's base is 5 m and its height 2 m. How is its area written?" options: ["10 m²", "10 m", "7 m²", "10 m³"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "m measures a length. Area counts squares: m².", "That adds.", "m³ is for volume."] explain: "5 × 2 = 10 square metres: 10 m²." - check: type: answer q: "Review: work out $4.5 \\times 6$." answer: "27" feedback: - ["24.5", "Multiply both parts: 4 × 6 + 0.5 × 6."] explain: "4 × 6 = 24 and 0.5 × 6 = 3: 27." ``` ### Base times height ### Ignore the slant ### Units ### Review: decimals ## Make: area 18, slanted ```step stage: make insight: "Building a slanted parallelogram with a given area means choosing a base and height that multiply to it, and seeing the slant does not matter." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#make", height: 560 } hint: ["Which pairs of numbers multiply to 18?", "Then move the top so it is not a rectangle."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a parallelogram that is not a rectangle, with area 18 cm².", when: "a = 18 and s^2 > 0", explain: "Base 6 and height 3, or base 9 and height 2, with the top moved along: any slant works." } ``` Then find a different base and height for the same area. ## Make: a slanted tile, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A slanted tile gives three lengths and one of them is a slanted side; the key step is choosing the perpendicular height, the one at a right angle to the base." hint: ["Which length meets the base at a right angle?", "Multiply the base by that height."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A tiler cuts slanted tiles. Each tile is a parallelogram with a base of 30 cm, a slanted side of 20 cm and a perpendicular height of 16 cm. What area of floor does one tile cover, in cm²?" steps: - ["Base 30 cm and perpendicular height 16 cm", "the slanted 20 cm is not at a right angle to the base"] - ["$A = b \\times h = 30 \\times 16$", "area is base × perpendicular height"] - ["$A = 480$ cm²", "area is in square centimetres"] picks: - step: 1 q: "Which length goes with the base?" options: - "The perpendicular height, 16 cm" - "The slanted side, 20 cm" - "Both, added: 36 cm" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The slanted side is longer than the height. Cut and move the triangle and it disappears.", "Adding lengths gives a perimeter idea. Area multiplies the base and the height."] answer: "480" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["600", "That uses the slanted side, 20 cm. Use the perpendicular height, 16 cm."] - ["46", "That adds the base and the height. Multiply them."] criteria: - "I chose the length at a right angle to the base." - "I ignored the slanted side." - "My answer is in cm²." explain: "30 × 16 = 480 cm². The slanted side, 20 cm, is extra information." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The tile is made up for the task. Sketch it, mark the right angle, say which length you ignore, and type the area. ```teacher summary: Students cut a parallelogram along its height and move the triangle to make a rectangle, see that sliding the top keeps the area, and use A = bh with the perpendicular height (AC9M7M01, node 1). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can explain why a parallelogram has the same area as a rectangle with the same base and height. - I can find the area of a parallelogram with base × perpendicular height. - I can tell the perpendicular height from a slanted side. struggle: Choosing the perpendicular height when a slanted side is also labelled. Ask students to trace the right-angle mark with a finger before they multiply, rather than telling them which number to use. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need area of rectangles by counting rows of squares (Year 6) and the meaning of cm². The one idea: a parallelogram rearranges into a rectangle with the same base and height, so A = bh. The common mistake is using the slanted side (Ruby's mistake); the board's dashed height with its right-angle mark is the fix. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Students who chose the parallelogram think longer sides mean more area." - "Run: ask where the cut went, and why there." - "Investigate: have students point to the height on the bug task's picture in their head: which length meets the base at a right angle?" - "Modify: for the missing height, ask what operation undoes × 6." - "Make: collect different base and height pairs for 18." - "Paper: the slanted tile is worked in books; the page marks the area and the reason for using the perpendicular height, then shows a model. Books out, and look for the 20 cm crossed out or labelled as extra." stuck: - see: A student multiplies by the slanted side (Ruby's mistake). ask: Which length meets the base at a right angle? fix: "Use the perpendicular height: the dashed line with the ∟." - see: A student adds base and height. ask: How many rows of squares, and how many in each row? fix: "Area is rows × squares in a row: multiply." - see: A student writes cm for an area. ask: Are we counting lengths or squares? fix: "Squares: cm²." stretch: Draw three different parallelograms on squared paper, each with area 24 cm², none of them a rectangle. support: Cut paper parallelograms and rearrange them; count squares on the board for small cases. leads: > Next: Area of triangles (node 1), half of a parallelogram. Where it leads: area of trapeziums and composite shapes (Year 8), and volume of prisms (the base times the height again). exit: q: A parallelogram has base 9 cm, slanted side 5 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm. Find its area. a: 9 × 4 = 36 cm² (the 5 cm slanted side is not used). explain: > A parallelogram is a rectangle pushed over. Cut the triangle off one end along the **perpendicular height** and move it to the other end: it becomes a rectangle with the same base and height. So: $$A = b \times h$$ where $h$ is the perpendicular height, at a right angle to the base, not the slanted side. Area is in square units: cm², m². ```
